audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.5%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.3%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.2%, il VIX è in aumento dell'1.9%. Il Dollar Index è in rialzo dello 0.3%, l'oro è stabile a 4714 dollari l'oncia. Il petrolio è in rialzo del 2.4% a 106.7 dollari. I rendimenti dei titoli di stato americani a 10 anni sono in rialzo dell'1.1% al 4.41%.

La presidente della BCE, Christine Lagarde, ha parlato di clima, natura e politica monetaria. Il presidente Trump incontrerà il leader cinese Xi Jinping per discutere questioni commerciali e di sicurezza, tra cui la guerra in Iran.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra gli ottantamila dollari con una variazione del 0,12%. I flussi ETF hanno registrato una uscita di 145,7 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle tensioni geopolitiche, come quelle tra Iran e Israele. 
  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum scende dell'1,86% a duemilatrecento dollari, mentre Solana guadagna lo 0,66% a novantacinque dollari e sessantaquattro centesimi. BNB invece registra un aumento dell'1,26% a seicentocinquantotto dollari e ventisette centesimi. 
  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 49, in zona neutrale, suggerisce quindi una sostanziale cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita. Per approfondire, trovate gli articoli sulla nostra piattaforma nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 0.5%, while Shanghai fell 0.3%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets. The S&P 500 closed up 0.2%, and the VIX is up 1.9%. The Dollar Index is up 0.3%, gold is essentially flat at $4,714 per ounce. Oil is up 2.4% at $106.7 US 10-year Treasury yields are up 1.1% at 4.41%. 

Christine Lagarde, ECB President, spoke about climate, nature, and monetary policy. President Trump will meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping to discuss trade and security issues, including the war in Iran. 

No major macroeconomic data releases are scheduled for today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin remains above eighty thousand dollars with a 0.12% change. ETF flows recorded an outflow of $145.7 million. This movement could be influenced by geopolitical tensions, such as those between Iran and Israel. 
Among altcoins, Ethereum falls 1.86% to $2,300, while Solana gains 0.66% to $95.64 BNB instead records a 1.26% increase to $658.27 
The Fear & Greed Index is at 49, in neutral territory, suggesting substantial caution among investors.

We are awaiting economic data releases on the markets. For more details, find the articles on our platform in the Top Stories section. Thanks for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Interest Rates Can’t Control Today’s Inflation
articles.snippet: Inflation is once again rising across advanced economies, driven by geopolitical turmoil, surging energy prices, and fragile supply chains rather than excess demand. Yet policymakers continue to treat it as a monetary problem, relying on a tool that cannot address the underlying causes.

articles.title: How to Win a Trade War: Book launch and discussion with Bown and Keynes
articles.snippet: Soumaya Keynes and Chad P. Bown discuss their new book How to Win a Trade War, available for pre-order. Trade wars are here to stay, and refusing to engage in the fight is no longer an option. President Donald Trump's tariff announcements can crash markets and sour decades-long alliances. China's export restrictions on rare earths could bring the West's car production to a crashing halt. Curbs on trade in cutting-edge chips could determine who wins the artificial intelligence (AI) race. From identifying supply chain vulnerabilities to installing stockpiles, subsidies, and trade restrictions,…

articles.title: Fentanyl, China, and Trump's 2025 tariffs
articles.snippet: Fentanyl abuse is a first-order public health crisis in the United States. In 2025, President Donald Trump imposed tariffs on China for its role in fentanyl trade, then raised them, lowered them, and in 2026 a Supreme Court decision eliminated them. But variations in tariff rates over 2025–26 cannot explain an epidemic that had already begun to recede when the second Trump administration took office. Fentanyl is a synthetic opioid, 50 times stronger than heroin and 100 times stronger than morphine. Drug overdoses—the bulk associated with fentanyl—were the leading cause of death among…

articles.title: The Other Border Problem: How Russia and China’s Lawfare Threaten the Arctic
articles.snippet: What happens when the Arctic starts to look like the South China Sea?Historically, a neutral region where cooperation prevailed, the Arctic is quickly becoming a contested space. articles.title: Closing the Gap? Italy Sets New Rules for Its First National Security Strategy Amidst Old Obstacles

Recently, however, domestic political consolidation and external pressures have appeared to align in a way not seen before. articles.title: China’s Teapot Refiners Slash Output as Hormuz Crisis Crushes Margins
articles.snippet: Some independent refiners in China are reducing their production rates as margins shrink and demand weakens amid the continued paralysis of tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. Citing unnamed trade and industry sources, Reuters reported today that the average operating rates at so-called teapots in Shandong had fallen to 50%, from 55% in April. What’s more, the operating rates of independent refiners are likely to fall further as the war drags on, and refiners swing into losses that the Reuters sources estimate at between $74 and $88 per…

articles.title: BP, Shell, TotalEnergies Pocket Billions in War-Driven Trading Windfall
articles.snippet: The European oil majors with the biggest trading desks raised their trading profits by up to $4.75 billion in the first quarter from the end of last year, amid extreme market volatility driven by the war in Iran. The biggest European majors, BP, Shell, and TotalEnergies, likely earned between $3.3 billion and $4.75 billion more in the first quarter compared to the fourth quarter of 2025, the Financial Times reports, citing estimates from analysts.
